$description: Hand-maintained audit of every sentence on approach.html (#497) — the one input to build-checks group 52 (claims), which re-derives every block from the page and fails on any sentence this file does not list. A copy change on approach.html re-pins its sentences here in the same PR (CLAUDE.md convention). BLOCKS: a block is the nearest non-inline ancestor of a text node inside <main> (inline: a abbr b button code dfn em i kbd mark q s small span strong sub sup time u br), so a navigation row is a block too; every block carries data-claim="<id>" on itself, and its sentences, joined with one space, equal its text (entities decoded, whitespace collapsed). One row = one sentence. KINDS: claim — states something the site can show; needs target, steps and how. label — names a page, section, card, button or list. definition — says what a term means. attribution — names a source. stance — a judgement or an aim stated as one, never a past fact or an outcome. Every non-claim needs a reason a reviewer reads; none has a target. TARGETS: #id (an id on this page); /path[#id] (a tracked file the site serves; an extensionless path is .html, and #id must be in that file); https://github.com/linardsb/ux-factory/{blob|tree}/main/<path> (a tracked repo path; a fragment only as a heading anchor on a blob .md, proven against the file's headings — a line range goes stale silently and is refused); control:<selector> (a chrome or /approach entry in system/param-manifest.json). STEPS: one click, toggle or navigation is one step; 0 means the target sits in the claim's own <section>. maxSteps is 2 and the gate pins it, so raising it is a gate edit, not a data edit. The gate verifies hop 1 — a link equal to the target in the claim's own block, or in the block named by via (same section) — and that the target resolves; the rest of the path is declared in how and walked by hand. RENDERED: the two proof lines a script writes, pinned by element id, source artifact and the literal fragments in the page source. CANNOT REACH: whether a sentence's kind is honest (a stance or definition hiding an unproven claim — a reviewer reads each reason), whether the hops after the first land where how says (the dock and the inspect toggle are walked by hand), whether a GitHub target renders on github.com (the gate proves the path is tracked and on disk, not that the push landed or the repo is public), the page's <head>, the injected chrome, glossary bubbles and any text a script renders (annotated-source, derive-probe, inspect), attribute text (aria-label, title, alt), which sentence of a block a link sits in (hop 1 is block-scoped, so a sentence may use a link in another sentence of its block, and its how says so), and every page but approach.html.

sentences.text: How I decide and pace work
Shape it
A vague ask becomes a scoped bet with a time budget.

sentences.text: How I make it work for real people
Design for behaviour
A feature only matters if someone actually uses it.
sentences.reason: a judgement about what makes a feature matter

sentences.text: I find the real trigger, cut the friction between the person and the payoff, and make the behaviour easier before trying to make it more motivating.

sentences.text: The aim is a feature people come back to without being nudged.

sentences.text: If a pattern lifts a metric by making someone feel worse, it doesn't ship.

sentences.text: How I know it worked
Prove it

The outcome I'm after is what changed for the person using it, so before building I write down what would show it worked: an early signal like activation, and the slower outcome behind it like retention.
